diagnoses.summary: PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations. The strongest evidence points to an H2 PCV (cstr_vent_valve) related fault causing reactor pressure control issues.
Abnormal PCA with coherent upset dominated by CSTR outlet/column feed and main bottom stream disruption; most likely Bottoms pump trip causing cascade through the plant.
Abnormal PCA with large coherent disturbance and widespread correlation breaks, dominated by CSTR pressure signal, consistent with an H2 PCV (CSTR vent) fault propagating through the system.
The PCA indicates a high-SPE, coherent upset centered on the CSTR pressure measurement and PCV control signals, consistent with H2 PCV impairment affecting reactor pressure control.
High SPE with a large, coherent shift along existing normal correlations; dominant contribution from reactor pressure measurement suggests a sensor issue rather than a pure process upset.

PCA detects a high SPE with coherent T² movement, dominated by a single pressure signal and related control valve activity. Most consistent with H2 PCV fault causing reactor pressure rise and a command-actual mismatch.
High SPE with coherent disturbance pointing to H2 PCV abnormalities affecting reactor pressure. Likely PCV actuator fault(s) rather than a random sensor issue.

A coherent plant upset with reactor pressure rising and PCV-related control actions active, most consistent with H2 PCV degradation or stiction affecting the vent valve, with a secondary possibility of a biased reactor pressure sensor.

PCA flags a large coherent upset with a strong SPE indicating a likely H2 PCV issue. Top contributors point at reactor pressure related to PCV control, with PCV being a plausible actuator fault driving the abnormal pattern.

PCA detects a coherent plant upset dominated by reactor pressure signal, with PCV (H2 purge) related controller and sensor variables driving the SPE. The strongest hints point to H2 PCV health issues causing abnormal pressure dynamics, potentially compounded by a biased pressure sensor.

The abnormal PCA state with simultaneous high Hotelling T² and high SPE, dominated by the CSTR pressure signal and PCV-related signals, strongly points to H2 PCV issues propagating through the system, likely IC valve degradation or blockage, rather than a simple sensor fault.

PCA detects a coherent plant upset with increased SPE, dominated by CSTR pressure signals and PCV-related control interactions. The most likely cause is an issue with the hydrogen PCV system or its pressure sensing, leading to abnormal reactor pressure correlations and PCV-command/actual mismatch.
